title: SATP event extraction, draft v1 (2026-11-24; v0 plus the gaps found coding 250 texts)
description: One object per SATP event text. Every *_verbatim field copies words from the text exactly, so later code can check them with a string match. Definitions and decision rules are in notes/satp-codebook.md.

text_status.description: Does the text report at least one new act? Section 1 of the codebook.

no_act_reason.description: Filled only when text_status is no_new_act.

fragment.description: True when the text cannot be read on its own (e.g. 'In the second incident', 'the blast appeared to be the handiwork of').

delayed_report.description: Text says 'according to a delayed report' or similar.

links.description: Earlier acts the text refers to (for linking and to stop double counts).

acts.description: One item per distinct act (different action, place or date). Recalled acts are listed too, with status recalled, so they can be dropped later.

status.description: new = first report of an act that happened on or near the report date; follow_up = new information on an earlier act that does not add a new act (identification, search for bodies, operation continuing); follow_up_adds_casualty = a victim of an earlier act died later (counts go to the earlier act, never a new event); recalled = mentioned as background; planned_or_threatened = not yet happened.

attempt_failed.description: Bomb did not explode, attack repulsed with no harm, kidnap bid foiled.

multi_site.description: One act spread over several places or districts (simultaneous raids, a bandh across districts). Resolve to the smallest unit that contains all sites.

secondary_sub_event_type.description: Second sub-type of the same act, e.g. an ambush in which rifles were also looted.

trigger_verbatim.description: The verb phrase that states the act, e.g. 'shot dead', 'were arrested', 'surrendered', 'recovered'.

sub_event_type.description: ACLED sub-types plus SATP additions marked +. +threat_or_diktat = a group threatens civilians over ethnicity, religion, dress or language (event); bans with no threat to people are not events.

conflict_reason_verbatim.description: Words that justify conflict_class (group name, stated motive).

disputed_account.description: Another party contests the official version (fake encounter claims, group denies).

more_actors_verbatim.description: Third and later actors on either side, verbatim.

identity_verbatim.description: Ethnic, religious or origin identity when the text gives it ('workers from Bihar', 'non-locals', 'Adivasi villagers').

intended.description: True for the intended target when the people hit were others (grenade aimed at a CRPF camp hit civilians).

cumulative_total_mentioned.description: Text gives a running toll; counts above hold only the new ones.

provisional.description: Bodies yet to be recovered, operation continuing, blood marks only, 'unconfirmed reports put the figure at five'.

report_date_verbatim.description: When the text separates the report or tweet date from the act date ('tweets ... on April 4', 'according to the media reports of April 18').

group_name.description: Short name from the actor list (CPI-Maoist, ULFA-I, NSCN-IM, HM, LeT, CRPF, Army, State Police...).

role.description: site = where the act happened; site_area = administrative area containing the site ('under X PS limits'); reference = a nearby place used to describe the site; route = the act happened on the way between named places; responding_ps = the police station whose team reached the spot (usually the jurisdiction); site_from_actor_unit = no place in the text, only the unit's home ('Delhi Police Special Cell'); the rest are not the act site.

parent_verbatim.description: The next larger unit named with it ('Raghunathnagar Police Station' for 'Sonhat village').
